clinician.trajectory_summary: A man in his 50s with a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation presented with 1 week of fever, nausea, vomiting, generalized weakness, confusion, back pain, urinary hesitancy, and lower extremity numbness and weakness. Initial workup revealed diffuse leptomeningitis on MRI brain, CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis, and elevated protein. Extensive infectious, metabolic, neoplastic, and preliminary autoimmune workup (including oligoclonal bands, ACE, AQP4, MOG) were negative. Meningeal and brain biopsy showed no evidence of infectious organisms. Due to rapidly progressive disease, pulse dose steroids (methylprednisolone 1000 mg IV daily for 5 days, then solumedrol 60 mg IV daily) were initiated, which prevented further clinical decline but did not improve lower extremity weakness. Several days later, CSF GFAP-IgG antibody testing returned positive at 1:128 (ref <1:2), confirming the diagnosis. Antimicrobials were stopped, and the patient underwent five sessions of plasmapheresis. Two weeks after a second MRI, he showed clinical and radiologic improvement, with lower extremity strength improving to 4/5 prior to discharge. At 3-month follow-up, he was ambulating with a cane with full strength throughout, aside from 4+/5 strength in the hip flexors bilaterally.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with symptoms consistent with meningomyeloencephalitis, including fever, confusion, and neurological deficits (myelopathy and leptomeningitis).
MRI brain showed diffuse leptomeningitis.
CSF analysis showed elevated white blood cells (85-501/mm3) with lymphocytic predominance (87%) and elevated protein (306 mg/dL).
Extensive infectious workup (CSF and serum) was negative.
Meningeal and brain biopsy showed no evidence of infectious organisms.
Preliminary autoimmune workup (oligoclonal bands, ACE, AQP4, MOG) was negative.

Patient was started on pulse dose steroids (methylprednisolone 1000 mg IV daily for 5 days, then solumedrol 60 mg IV daily) which prevented further clinical decline but did not improve lower extremity weakness.
CSF autoimmune encephalitis panel returned positive for GFAP 1:128 (ref <1:2).
Following GFAP positivity, antimicrobials were stopped, and the patient underwent five sessions of plasmapheresis.
Two weeks after the second MRI, the patient had clinical and radiologic improvement.
Prior to discharge, patient’s strength improved to 4/5 in the lower extremities.
At 3-month follow-up, the patient was ambulating with a cane with full strength throughout, aside from 4+/5 strength in the hip flexors bilaterally.
